requirements.text: create a problem record to analyze the database communication breakdown ... Both impact and urgency should be set to high, and assign the problem to Travis Wood
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_011' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND assigned_to = 'USER_011' AND category = 'database' AND status = 'new'
requirements.source: Verify problem assignment to Travis Wood for Oracle DB outage
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (PRB_011 after PRB_010); the only problem the task creates
Travis Wood resolves to USER_011, the only user of that name in the seed (active, role agent)
priority critical from the policy's problem matrix (section 4.2): impact high x urgency high
status new from the policy's default for new problems (section 4.2)
category database kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, but the request's 'database communication breakdown' and the source incident's category (database) support it
opened_by, org_id, assignment_group, service and the problem_statement wording are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested
the acting user USER_004 is a manager, so may create problems (policy section 2)

requirements.text: Earlier today, a major incident oracle DB not responding ... create a problem record to analyze the database communication breakdown
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_011' AND original_task = 'INC_001'
requirements.source: Verify incident–problem linkage for Oracle DB outage
assumptions: the incident is INC_001, the only seed incident whose description is 'Oracle DB not responding. Major outage declared.' (short_description 'MAJOR:SAP Database Unreachable')
original_task kept from the benchmark check; the request names the incident as the problem's origin

disagreement: form: A tests original_task in its own requirement under the linkage check, B folds it into the create requirement's cells; kept A's split so each benchmark check has a requirement that carries it

requirements.text: a major incident oracle DB not responding ... create a problem record (policy 4.2: the Problem record must link all affected Incidents)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_001' AND problem = 'PRB_011'
source: Verify problem assignment to Travis Wood for Oracle DB outage
Verify incident–problem linkage for Oracle DB outage
assumptions: linking the affected incident is required by policy 4.2; the schema has no incident_to_problem table, so the link is incident.problem, written by update_incident (in tools)
the new problem's id assumed next in sequence (PRB_011)
both benchmark checks join incident.problem = problem.problem_id, so both are carried jointly by this requirement and the problem requirements

requirements.text: create a problem record ... assign the problem to Travis Wood
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_001' AND original_task = 'INC_001' AND assigned_to = 'USER_059' AND status = 'fix_in_progress'
assumptions: boundary: the seed already holds PRB_001 for INC_001 (category database, impact and urgency high, assigned to USER_059); the request asks for a new problem record, so a loose reading that reassigns PRB_001 to Travis Wood instead of creating one would break this
a run that reassigns PRB_001 and links INC_001 to it would pass the benchmark's first check, so this stay is what separates the two readings

requirements.text: a major incident oracle DB not responding (one incident; not the other SAP incidents)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id <> 'INC_001' AND problem = 'PRB_011'
assumptions: boundary of the incident selector: the request names one major incident; the other open SAP incidents on SVC_017 (INC_044, INC_069, INC_082) are not the Oracle outage and stay unlinked

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every value (PRB_011, USER_011, INC_001, priority critical, status new, category database) and on both dispositions (kept). disagreement: form: A carries the linkage check in two requirements (the problem's original_task and the incident's problem column), B folds original_task into the single create requirement; kept A's split, and named both benchmark checks as the source of the incident link, since both join incident.problem = problem.problem_id (logged in requirement 2). disagreement: stay on PRB_001 (A only); kept because the seed already holds a problem for INC_001 with the same category, impact and urgency, so reassigning it is the loose reading of 'create a problem record' and would pass the benchmark's first check. disagreement: stay on the other SAP incidents staying unlinked (B only); kept because policy 4.2 ('link all affected Incidents') invites a loose reading that sweeps the other SVC_017 incidents in, and the request names one incident. Seed facts re-checked at merge: Travis Wood is USER_011 (active, agent, ORG_001); the acting user USER_004 is a manager; no incident has its problem column set, so both benchmark checks are 0 on the seed; PRB_010 is the highest problem. opened_by (NOT NULL in the schema) is not tested: the request does not state it and the policy names opened_by only for incidents; both passes left it out. revised: the stay on PRB_001 named assigned_to and status in both its selector and its cells; the selector now names the row (PRB_001, original task INC_001) and the cells carry the two values that must not change, with the same count. revised: the stay on other incidents named problem = 'PRB_011' in both its selector and its cells; the selector now names the rows (every incident other than INC_001) and the cell carries the link that must stay absent, with the same count.
